story: Retired Indian resident, non-resident alien, no US days, files Form 1040-NR with a W-8BEN. US Social Security $24,000, IRA distributions $40,000, pension $20,000, US dividends $10,000 (W-8BEN claims the treaty's 25% dividend rate) and interest of $5,000 on a private loan to a US company the retiree part-owns (not bank-deposit or portfolio interest, which s.871(h)/(i) would exempt; no treaty claim filed for it).

expect.why: DTAA Art. 20(2): US Social Security paid to an Indian resident is taxable only in the US; s.871(a)(3) taxes 85% x 24,000 at 30%
per income type: dividends 25% (Art. 10 claim) x 10,000 = 2,500; interest has no claim, so 30% x 5,000 = 1,500 (the dividend claim no longer sets the rate for all FDAP)
DTAA Art. 20(1): periodic US pension and IRA payments are taxable only in India

expect.value: 1040-NR: FDAP taxed per income type, ECI at graduated rates
expect.why: dividends 25% and interest 30% — no single flat rate to show (a blended 27% is a rate nothing is taxed at)
no treaty position is taken in India (no US tie-break, no forced NR, no DTAA elections): a 1040-NR filer claims US treaty rates with a W-8BEN, so the Indian TRC/Form 41 alert must not fire
DTAA Art. 20(2): US Social Security is taxable only in the US — the Indian return must show it as exempt and claim no credit
W-8BEN is on file, so the payers can pay the Art. 20(1)-exempt pension without withholding
